units.title: Adventure
units.intro: Grammar: -ing words used like nouns (gerunds), to + verb (infinitives), -ing and -ed describing words, and will be + -ing (future continuous).

cards.title: Gerunds, infinitives and participles
rule: **Step 1 – after some verbs use -ing:** *enjoy, avoid, finish, mind, can't help*: *I enjoy **climbing** Emba Soira.*
**Step 2 – after other verbs use to + verb:** *want, decide, hope, plan, agree, attempt*: *We decided **to camp** near Filfil.*
**Step 3 – after a small word like in, at, of, about, without, use -ing:** *She is good **at drawing**.*
**to + verb** can also tell **why** (purpose): *She went to the market **to buy** berbere.*
**-ing or -ed?** The thing that **causes** the feeling takes **-ing**: *an **amazing** trip*. The person who **has** the feeling takes **-ed**: *We were **amazed***.

examples.text: The story was horrifying; we were horrified.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: I feel like _______ to the library.
cards.why: The phrasal verb **'feel like'** is always followed by a **gerund** (the -ing form of the verb). It is used to express a desire or inclination to do something.

cards.title: Step by step: -ing or to + verb?
cards.problem: Complete: (a) We enjoy ____ (walk) along the beach in Massawa. (b) They decided ____ (travel) to Nakfa by bus. (c) She is interested in ____ (learn) Arabic. (d) He went to the market ____ (buy) coffee beans. (e) The football match was ____ (excite); we were all ____ (excite).

steps.text: **Step 1: Look at the word just before the gap.**
**Step 3: want / decide / hope / plan → to + verb.** (b) decided **to travel**.
**Step 4: a small word like in / at / of / about → -ing.** (c) interested in **learning**.
**Step 5: Why did he go? → to + verb (purpose).** (d) **to buy**.
**Step 6: cause → -ing, feeling → -ed.** (e) The match was **exciting**; we were **excited**.

cards.answer: (a) walking (b) to travel (c) learning (d) to buy (e) exciting, excited

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: My grandfather finished ____ the field before the rain came.
cards.why:
**Step 1:** The word before the gap is *finished*.

**Step 2:** *finish* is always followed by **-ing** → **ploughing**.

**Step 3:** *to plough* follows verbs like *want, decide, hope* – not *finish*.

**Tip:** After enjoy / avoid / finish → -ing. After want / decide / hope → to + verb. After in / at / of / about → -ing. -ing word = the cause, -ed word = the feeling. will be + -ing = in the middle of an action at a future time.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: We hope ____ Emba Soira next summer.
cards.why:
**Step 1:** The word before the gap is *hope*.

**Step 2:** *hope* is followed by **to + verb** → **to climb**.

**Step 3:** ✗ *hope climbing* is not English.

**Tip:** After enjoy / avoid / finish → -ing. After want / decide / hope → to + verb. After in / at / of / about → -ing. -ing word = the cause, -ed word = the feeling. will be + -ing = in the middle of an action at a future time.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: The long walk to Debre Bizen was very ____.
cards.why:
**Step 1:** The walk is the **thing** that causes the feeling.

**Step 2:** cause → **-ing**: *tiring*.

**Step 3:** The people feel **tired** (-ed): *We were tired after the tiring walk.*

**Tip:** After enjoy / avoid / finish → -ing. After want / decide / hope → to + verb. After in / at / of / about → -ing. -ing word = the cause, -ed word = the feeling. will be + -ing = in the middle of an action at a future time.

cards.title: Future continuous
rule: **will be + verb-ing** = an action will be **in the middle** of happening at a future time: *This time tomorrow we **will be travelling** to Massawa.*
It is also a polite way to ask about plans: ***Will** you **be using** the computer tonight?*

examples.text: At 8 tomorrow I will be travelling to Keren.

examples.fix: At 8 tomorrow I will be travelling.

cards.title: Find and correct the error
cards.problem: Find and correct the error: "At 8 tomorrow I will travelling."

steps.text: **Step 1: Remember the form.** It has three parts: **will + be + verb-ing**.
**Step 2: Test the sentence.** *will travelling* has *will* and *-ing*, but **be** is missing.
**Step 3: Correct it.** *At 8 tomorrow I **will be travelling**.*

cards.answer: At 8 tomorrow I will be travelling.

cards.title: Memory tip
body: **After in / at / of / about, always -ing.** The **-ing** thing causes the **-ed** feeling.

cards.title: Unit summary
body: -ing words can work like nouns and come after enjoy / avoid / finish and after in / at / of. to + verb comes after want / decide / hope and tells why. -ing describes the cause, -ed the feeling. will be + -ing = in the middle of an action at a future time.

cards.title: Step by step: Future continuous
body: **Step 1:** Form: will + be + verb-ing: "I will be studying." Negative: won't be + -ing. Question: Will you be + -ing?
**Step 2:** Use 1: an action that will be going on at a time in the future: "At 8 pm tomorrow I will be watching the match."
**Step 3:** Use 2: a longer action that will be going on when something short happens: "When you arrive, we will be having dinner."
**Step 4:** Use 3: polite questions about someone's plans: "Will you be using the computer this evening?"
**Step 5:** Time words: this time tomorrow, at 6 o'clock next Monday, this time next week. Do not use it with state verbs (know, like, own).
**Example:** "This time next year, Aman ___ (study) at college." → will be studying. "Don't phone at 7; I ___ (cook)." → will be cooking.

cards.title: Mnemonic — "WILL BE + ING = a film paused in the future"
body: picture the action in the middle at that future time.

cards.title: Exam tip
body: Look for "at this time tomorrow / at (time) next…" in the question – these phrases almost always signal the future continuous.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: This time next week, I ____ on the beach in Massawa.
cards.why:
**Step 1:** "This time next week" is a point in the future.

**Step 2:** An action in progress then uses the future continuous.

**Step 3:** will be + -ing: will be lying.

**Tip:** After enjoy / avoid / finish → -ing. After want / decide / hope → to + verb. After in / at / of / about → -ing. -ing word = the cause, -ed word = the feeling. will be + -ing = in the middle of an action at a future time.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Which sentence uses the future continuous correctly?

options.A: At ten o'clock tomorrow she be taking her exam.
options.B: At ten o'clock tomorrow she will be take her exam.
options.C: At ten o'clock tomorrow she will be taking her exam.
options.D: At ten o'clock tomorrow she will taking her exam.

cards.why:
**Step 1:** The form is will + be + -ing.

**Step 2:** Only option C has all three parts.

**Step 3:** The others miss "be", miss "-ing" or miss "will".

**Tip:** After enjoy / avoid / finish → -ing. After want / decide / hope → to + verb. After in / at / of / about → -ing. -ing word = the cause, -ed word = the feeling. will be + -ing = in the middle of an action at a future time.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: "Don't phone me at 7. I ____ dinner then."
cards.why:
**Step 1:** At 7 the meal will be in progress.

**Step 2:** Future continuous: will be having.

**Step 3:** "will have had" would mean dinner is already over.

**Tip:** After enjoy / avoid / finish → -ing. After want / decide / hope → to + verb. After in / at / of / about → -ing. -ing word = the cause, -ed word = the feeling. will be + -ing = in the middle of an action at a future time.

glossary.meaning: A verb + -ing used like a noun (a thing): Swimming is fun.
to + the plain verb: to go, to camp.
will be + verb-ing: an action that will be in the middle of happening at a future time.

tips.text: **After in / at / of / about, always -ing.** The **-ing** thing causes the **-ed** feeling.
